Cutting the handle creates corners along the middle disk edge, so the old smooth cap argument was invalid. The repair retains cornered pairs, absorbs their distinguished face collars by a positive-derivative interval map, and straightens only after gluing; Wall §§2.6–2.7 supplies the checked quadrant and face-collar constructions. The claim and disk identification are unchanged.

The actual Statement explicitly promises adaptation only on two truncated collars and a noncritical corner band, not an adapted triad with constant whole boundary components. Direct differentiation gives F_a<0 when B<1 and F_b=1 when B=1; the two axes and quadratic origin cover the remaining points. The connected-boundary example therefore does not contradict any stated conclusion; no edit is licensed.

F6 omitted the supplied n=0 convention and falsely typed empty faces as dimension -1. It now restricts the dimension assertion to n>=1 and records empty faces/collars for n=0. In that case U0=U1=empty, U2=W, h=1/2, and the critical-point-free boundary neighbourhood is empty, so the unchanged proof and Statement remain valid.

F4 overstated the abstract supplier: it does not promise the prescribed embedding or fix the incoming face. F4 is corrected, and the explicit attaching-data check establishes the core and y framing under explicit quadratic flow, radial tube expansion, compact local modification, and collar absorption fixed near the incoming end. Step 1.1 now also uses compactness to confine the height change to the specified outgoing strip. Wall Theorem 5.1.9 and its 5.1.6 proof were read in full.

The old proof inferred identity near M0 from abstract attachment diffeomorphism types. It now builds local chart-supported modifications and cutoff normalized flows on compact interior bands, absorbs collars with interval maps fixed at their inner edges, and only then extends the resulting maps by identity. Simultaneous charts have disjoint support, and a common pushed-in lower copy supplies the claimed homotopy of pairs; the Statement is unchanged.

A regular fibre in dimension zero is empty, and the old assertion 2 incorrectly called it a dimension -1 manifold. The repair keeps dimension zero in scope, explicitly assigns empty crossing sets and empty product maps there, and proves this case before the unchanged positive-dimensional flow and framing argument. No positive-dimensional conclusion or trajectory interface is weakened.

F4 incorrectly placed M×[0,1] in the boundaryless smooth-manifold category. It now distinguishes the boundaryless factor and faces from the product boundary charts on W and cites the boundary-map category. Step 2.1 explicitly rescales to the actual initial collar width epsilon and has a smooth inverse fixing the incoming face. The example and empty handle claim are unchanged.

An isolated critical value may also carry other indices: a torus with its two saddles at c disjoint from a sphere with minimum c satisfies the old hypotheses, but crossing c creates a component and cannot attach only 1-handles. The repaired Statement explicitly excludes other indices at c, the mathematically necessary missing hypothesis. The proof uses compact interior support rather than avoidance of the entire fixed collar and retains the disjoint-attachment and isotopy conclusions.

The old step 2.1 falsely inferred that a two-critical-level band avoids the entire fixed regular boundary collar; a separate product component can make that collar meet every intervening level. The repair uses only 0<a<d<1, which makes the band a compact interior set and hence disjoint from a smaller boundary neighbourhood. The finite collection of such supports leaves a common boundary neighbourhood fixed, while the small field perturbations preserve descent for the original function and bubble-sort termination is unchanged.

ledger_updates.subject: lem-gradient-like-perturbation-separates-adjacent-critical-levels
ledger_updates.finding: F2: each of these spheres carries a product neighbourhood in the closed $(n-1)$-manifold $f^{-1}(v)$; Proof 1.1 repeats that type assertion for n=0.
ledger_updates.affected_use: [F2] [[lem-spheres-of-adjacent-critical-levels-have-product-neighbourhoods]]: Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. Let $f$ be adapted on a compact triad with field $X$ and let $P$ (value $c$), $Q$ (value $c'>c$) be consecutive critical levels with $v\in(c,c')$ regular. Then for each $q\in Q$ the crossing set $A_q\subseteq f^{-1}(v)$ of the trajectories through the local unstable disk $D_q$ is a compact embedded sphere of dimension $\operatorname{ind}(q)-1$, and for each $p\in P$ the crossing set $B_p$ of the trajectories through the local stable disk $E_p$ is a compact embedded sphere of dimension $n-\operatorname{ind}(p)-1$, with $A_q=\varnothing$ when $\operatorname{ind}(q)=0$ and $B_p=\varnothing$ when $\operatorname{ind}(p)=n$; each of these spheres carries a product neighbourhood in the closed $(n-1)$-manifold $f^{-1}(v)$. A trajectory has a limit in $Q$ exactly when it passes through the local unstable disk of that limit and a limit in $P$ exactly when it passes through the local stable disk of that limit, so a trajectory whose limits lie in $Q$ and $P$ crosses $f^{-1}(v)$ exactly once, at a point of $A_q\cap B_p$, and every point of $A_q\cap B_p$ lies on such a trajectory.
ledger_updates.minimality: Add the n=0 empty-fibre/empty-set case to F2 and Proof 1.1, before the positive-dimensional argument; do not alter the Statement.

downstream_reviews.affected_use:
The non-canonicity is exhibited piece by piece by the items of this page. The
correspondence between Morse functions and presentations,
[[thm-morse-functions-and-handle-decompositions-correspond]], produces a
presentation from any adapted excellent Morse function, and different
functions, fields and admissible attaching embeddings can give different presentations of the
same $W$. Negating the function replaces every presentation by its dual,
[[thm-handle-duality-from-negating-a-morse-function]], reversing the order of
the handles and exchanging attaching and belt spheres. Rearranging the critical
levels by index, [[thm-morse-rearrangement-by-index]], and passing to a
self-indexed function, [[thm-self-indexing-morse-function-existence]], changes
the order in which the handles are attached and groups the handles of one index
at a single level, without changing $W$; reordering equal-index handles and
replacing an attaching embedding by an isotopic one is covered by
[[lem-handles-of-equal-index-can-be-attached-on-one-level]]. The two endpoint
eliminations, [[prop-connected-cobordisms-admit-presentations-without-superfluous-zero-handles]]
and [[prop-dual-elimination-of-top-index-handles]], delete or retain handles of
extreme index according to the incoming and outgoing boundary, so even the
number of handles in a presentation depends on the boundary data. Finally the
empty presentation of a product,
[[lem-product-cobordisms-have-critical-point-free-presentations|the product
presentation]], and the corner-rounding conventions of
[[def-attaching-a-smooth-handle-with-corner-rounding]] show that the attaching
data themselves are a choice: the framing and the rounding of a handle are part
of its presentation. Compatible changes of rounding preserve the diffeomorphism
type; changing a framing is different attaching data and can change that type.

interface_changes.original:
Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. Let $(W;M_0,M_1)$ be a compact triad and let $f$ be
an adapted Morse function whose critical points of index $k$ all lie at one
level $c$, with no other critical value in a neighbourhood of $c$. Then the
sublevel just above $c$ is obtained from the sublevel just below $c$ by
attaching disjoint $k$-handles, one for each index-$k$ critical point.
Equivalently, handles of equal index attached at one level may be regarded as
attached simultaneously or successively in any order, the result being the same
up to diffeomorphism fixing the incoming face and respecting the lower sublevel up to homotopy of pairs. On the common attached-stage model, reordering disjoint attachments fixes its entire lower stage. Handles of equal index may
be reordered freely, and attaching embeddings may be changed by isotopy of the
attaching region.

interface_changes.original:
A **smooth cobordism triad** $(W;M_0,M_1)$ consists of the following data.

- A compact smooth $n$-manifold with boundary $W$
  ([[def-topological-manifold-with-boundary]],
  [[def-smooth-chart-atlas-and-structure-on-a-manifold-with-boundary]],
  [[def-compact-space]]).
- For $n\ge1$, two closed embedded smooth $(n-1)$-submanifolds
  $M_0,M_1\subseteq\partial W$ with $\partial W=M_0\sqcup M_1$
  ([[def-interior-point-boundary-point-interior-and-boundary-of-a-manifold]],
  [[thm-the-boundary-is-a-closed-embedded-smooth-n-minus-one-manifold]],
  [[def-embedded-smooth-submanifold-with-boundary]]).
- Fixed collars of both faces in $W$
  ([[def-smooth-collar-of-a-manifold-boundary]]), whose existence is
  [[thm-collar-neighborhood-theorem]].

For $n=0$, the convention is $\partial W=M_0=M_1=\varnothing$: a zero-dimensional manifold has discrete point charts and empty boundary. The two collar domains are empty and their unique maps supply the collar data. No manifold of dimension $-1$ is introduced. Reversal retains the same empty faces.

The two faces are the **incoming** face $M_0$ and the **outgoing** face $M_1$;
they are disjoint by the decomposition $\partial W=M_0\sqcup M_1$ fixed by
the data. Each face is a union of boundary components and need not be connected. Either face may
be empty: $\partial W=\varnothing$ with $M_0=M_1=\varnothing$ is allowed, and so
is $M_0=\varnothing$, $M_1=\partial W$. All smooth maps between manifolds with
boundary are the ones of
[[def-smooth-map-between-manifolds-with-boundary]], and all diffeomorphisms
below are diffeomorphisms of that category.

The **reversed triad** of $(W;M_0,M_1)$ is $(W;M_1,M_0)$: it carries the same
manifold $W$ with the two faces exchanged and with the same fixed collars, read
with the opposite roles.

No orientation is required, and an orientation, when present, is extra
structure: no statement on this page uses one unless it is listed among the
hypotheses.

is $M_0=\varnothing$, $M_1=\partial W$. All smooth maps between manifolds with
boundary are the ones of
[[def-smooth-map-between-manifolds-with-boundary]], and all diffeomorphisms
below are diffeomorphisms of that category.

The **reversed triad** of $(W;M_0,M_1)$ is $(W;M_1,M_0)$: it carries the same
manifold $W$ with the two faces exchanged and with the same fixed collars, read
with the opposite roles.

No orientation is required, and an orientation, when present, is extra
structure: no statement on this page uses one unless it is listed among the
hypotheses.
